blocks.html: Larger overlap means larger $t$: a wider band and a smaller effective mass. Near the band top ($k=\pi/a$) the curvature is negative: $m^*=-\hbar^2/2ta^2$.

enc.title: Formula cards: diatomic chain, which sign is which branch

blocks.html: The diatomic dispersion has a $\pm$ in front of the root. The root is never negative, so the minus sign always gives the lower branch and the plus sign the upper branch: minus = acoustic (it starts at $\omega=0$ for $q=0$: the whole crystal moves together, a sound wave), plus = optical (finite frequency already at $q=0$: the two atoms of a cell move against each other). Quick test in an exam: put $q=0$; the sign that gives $\omega=0$ is the acoustic one.

blocks.label: Diatomic chain: minus = acoustic, plus = optical, script (2.37)
Diatomic chain limits: q→0 and the zone edge (gap)

blocks.html: Where the limits come from: with $S=\frac1{M_1}+\frac1{M_2}$, for small $q$ the root is $\approx S-\frac{q^2a^2}{2M_1M_2S}$ and $M_1M_2S=M_1+M_2$; at $qa=\pi$, $1-\cos qa=2$ and the root becomes $\big|\frac1{M_1}-\frac1{M_2}\big|$. Motion: at $q=0$ acoustic all in phase, optical $M_1U=-M_2V$; at the zone edge only the heavy atoms move (acoustic) or only the light ones (optical), neighbouring cells in antiphase (standing wave). Try it in the experiment station of this room.

check.q: In $\omega^2=k(\frac1{M_1}+\frac1{M_2})\pm k\sqrt{\dots}$, which sign gives the acoustic branch?
check.explain: At $q=0$ the root equals $\frac1{M_1}+\frac1{M_2}$, so the minus sign gives $\omega=0$: the acoustic branch.

check.explain: The root becomes $|\frac1{M_1}-\frac1{M_2}|$; plus gives $2k/M_{\rm light}$, minus $2k/M_{\rm heavy}$.

check.q: How do the two atoms of a cell move in the optical mode at $q=0$?
options: against each other, $M_1U=-M_2V$ (centre of mass at rest)
check.explain: In phase together is the acoustic mode at $q=0$; one sublattice only happens at the zone edge.
